startingLifestyle._source: Cyberpunk RED Core Rulebook p.109 (chargen), p.377-378 (Lifestyle & Housing), p.181 (Exec Teamwork Role Ability)
startingLifestyle.firstMonthNote: Characters get their starting housing and Lifestyle free for the first month. Rent and Lifestyle are due from month two.
startingLifestyle.lifestyleFailureNote: If Lifestyle is unpaid at the start of a month, the Character has one week, then rolls a Death Save at the start of each unpaid day.

execProvision.rule: The Exec's Teamwork Role Ability grants Corporate Housing at Rank 2. Every Character starts with their Role Ability at Rank 4, so an Exec DOES receive it at character creation.
execProvision.rentNote: Given by the Corporation. No rent or fees while they remain a member. If they move to another Corporation, the new one extends the same offer and pays to move their belongings.
execProvision.lifestyleNote: The Exec must still buy their own Lifestyle separately every month — housing is free, food is not.

humanity._source: Cyberpunk RED Core Rulebook p.80 (Humanity STAT), p.230 (Cyberpsychosis)
humanity.empFromHumanity: floor(Humanity / 10) - EMP drops each time the tens place of Humanity drops (44 HUM = EMP 4; 39 HUM = EMP 3)
humanity.cyberpsychosisNote: Cyberpsychosis triggers when Humanity drops BELOW zero (HUM < 0). Exactly 0 is not yet cyberpsychosis. There is no intermediate mechanical warning band in RAW; low EMP is described as narratively predisposing but carries no separate threshold.

traumaHumanityLoss.example: Witnessing a particularly horrific death or mutilation
Starvation, war zone, month of constant danger

humanity._note: Trauma losses are GM-driven and belong to the play loop, not chargen. Included here so the engine has one authoritative Humanity source.
humanity.clampNote: Humanity is NOT clamped at 0. RAW (p.80) says cyberpsychosis triggers when HUM 'drops below zero', which requires negative values to exist. Clamping at 0 makes the cyberpsychosis flag unreachable. Track the true (possibly negative) value for threshold logic and floor only the DISPLAY value at 0.
humanity.empFloorNote: EMP derived from Humanity is floored at 0 — negative Humanity must not produce a negative EMP.

statDescriptions._source: Cyberpunk RED Core Rulebook p.72 (STAT definitions). `description` is the book's own wording, condensed only by removing line-break artifacts. `drives` is a plain-language UI summary of what the STAT governs mechanically — written for players, derived from the rules but not printed verbatim.

int.name: Intelligence
int.description: How generally bright you are. As a rule, this is more than sheer intelligence, but also includes cleverness, awareness, perception, and your ability to learn.
int.drives: Perception, Education, and most knowledge Skills.

will.name: Willpower
will.description: Your determination and ability to face danger and/or stress. This STAT also represents your courage and ability to survive long-term privation. This STAT is important for determining how much damage you can take.
will.drives: Resisting fear and stress. With BODY, sets Hit Points.

cool.name: Cool
cool.description: Your ability to impress and influence people through your character and charisma; how well you get along with others; how you interact in social situations.

emp.name: Empathy
emp.description: Your ability to relate to and care for others, and take others into consideration. Particularly important as it offsets the effects of cyberpsychosis, a dangerous mental illness common in the Dark Future.
emp.drives: Reading and relating to people. Sets your starting Humanity (EMP x 10).

tech.name: Technique
tech.description: Your ability to manipulate tools or instruments. This is not the same as Reflexes, inasmuch as this covers the knack of using tools. One Character might have a high Technique but might not be able to fence or juggle. On the other hand, another might have high Reflexes, but might not be able to rewire a computer or hot-wire a car.

ref.name: Reflexes
ref.description: Your response time and coordination, as used in aiming, throwing, juggling, etc. A stage magician, for example, would have a high Reflex STAT. Most importantly, this is the STAT that affects your ability to hit things with ranged weapons.

luck.name: Luck
luck.description: How the gods of chance see you. With a high enough Luck, you can tip the scales in your favor. In a game mechanics sense, you can apply points from this STAT to offset die rolls in your favor. However, this pool of points only refills at the beginning of the next session.
luck.drives: A refreshing pool of points you can spend to boost your own rolls.

body.name: Body
body.description: Your size, toughness, and ability to stay alive and conscious due to physical mass, structure, or other qualities. This STAT is important for determining how much damage you can take.
body.drives: Melee damage, Death Save, and with WILL, Hit Points.

dex.name: Dexterity
dex.description: Your overall physical competence, as it pertains to balancing, leaping, jumping, combat, and other athletic activities. A gymnast would have a high Dexterity. Most importantly, this is the STAT that affects your ability to hit things with melee weapons and can help you dodge attacks.
dex.drives: Melee attack Skills, Evasion, and Athletics.

move.name: Movement
move.description: Your speed of movement: running, leaping, swimming, etc.
move.drives: How far you travel in a Turn, and jumping distance.

statDescriptions._hyphenNote: Line-break hyphens in the source are ambiguous. Of five joins in this section, four are correct as joined (competence, coordination, inasmuch, represents); 'long-term' required its hyphen restored.
